parsed.modern: the country in their time was entirely cleared, or definitely divided ; the fields were forwarded by woods, not by hedges , and if a confidential trait of improved land lay together, it fill was not separated into a number of inclosures. The subjects, therefore, proper to receive this character, are those in which cultivation seems to have encroached on the wild, not to have subdued it ; as the bottom of a valley in corn, while the sides are still overgrown with wood ; and the outline of that wood indented by the village creeping more or left up the hill. But a glade of grass, thus circumstanced, does not peculiarly belong to the species that may occur in a park or pastoral farm ; in this, the pastures should rather border on a wald or a common : if large, they may be broken by flagging yellow, thickets, or coppices ; and the scattered trees should be beset with brables and briers. All these are circumstances which improve the beauty of the place : yet appear to be only remains of the wild, not intended for embellishment. Such interruptions must, however, be less frequent in the arable parts of the farm ; but there the opening may be divided into several lands, distinguished, as in common fields, only by different sorts of grain. These will sufficiently break the sameness of the space : and tillage does not furnish a more pleasing scene, than such a space so broken, if the extent be moderate, and the boundary beautiful.
